description: A version is proposed only once it has been public for seven days, so that a release pulled or fixed in its first week never reaches a branch. internalChecksFilter is already strict by default; it is stated so that the wait is read here as holding back the branch and the pull request themselves, not only a status check on them

customManagers.description: The Node of the images' base is read as a Node release rather than as a Docker tag. A tag such as 24.12.0-bookworm-slim is pushed again each time its Debian layer is rebuilt, so its time is not when that Node came out, and Docker Hub does not always give a time at all; without one, the seven-day wait holds the image back for good while setup-node moves on alone. Read from the Node releases, both carry the same time and so are let through on the same day. The variant after the version is kept as written

sdctl, which natsumi draws with (ADR 0044), is built into the workspace image by go install at a fixed version, since its releases carry no binary. No manager reads a version written on a go install line, so it is read here as the Go module it is

packageRules.description: Patch, digest and pinning updates are merged by Renovate itself once the pull request's checks pass, which are ci.yml's: the type check, the tests, the build and the browser's tests, run on every pull request. platformAutomerge is off so that the merge waits for those checks without relying on the repository's auto-merge setting or branch protection. Minor and major updates only open a pull request. What Renovate alone merged is released once a week by weekly-release.yml

The Node the images run (the Dockerfile's base) and the Node the checks run (setup-node in ci.yml and images.yml) are the same version on purpose: a test passing on one Node says little about another. Grouping them puts all of them on one branch, so they cannot drift apart one pull request at a time
The same Node is read by the custom manager above, from the Node releases. Left on, the dockerfile manager would propose it a second time under the Docker tag's times

@types/node describes the Node the code runs on, and its major follows Node's. A new major of it arrives before that Node is an LTS release the images can take, and type-checking against it would accept APIs the runtime lacks. Its major is raised by hand together with the node group

pi-coding-agent is built on pi-ai and names it as a dependency of its own, and natsumi imports both. They are released together under the same version, and a pi-ai left behind by one pull request would be installed twice. Grouping them moves them on one branch

The tools natsumi hands to Pi describe their parameters with typebox, and Pi's packages pin typebox to one exact version. Raised alone, it would put a second typebox beside Pi's; it is moved by hand to the version Pi names, when the pi group arrives with a new one

The images named in the compose files are the ones built from this checkout under a local tag, and the published images are pinned by the environment's settings (ADR 0033), whose repository is where Renovate moves them. A local tag is no version, which Renovate already skips; this keeps them out should a version ever be written here

Workflows are already read by the github-actions manager. Grouping them keeps a handful of actions from arriving as a handful of pull requests, since they are updated together and reviewed the same way. The Node of setup-node stays in the node group
